— 공자
ko.description:
**공자 · 논어 · I.1.2**

앞면은 아래 인용 원문을 직접 번역한 문장입니다. 해설·질문·관계는 편집 내용입니다.

### 맥락

논어의 첫 장은 배움의 기쁨에 이어 멀리서 오는 벗을 맞는 즐거움을 말한다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

오래 만나지 못한 친구와 시간을 보낼 때 꼭 유익한 정보를 얻거나 어떤 일을 해결해야 만남이 가치 있는 것은 아니다. 함께 배웠던 일을 떠올리고 달라진 생각을 듣는 것만으로도 의미가 생길 수 있다. 이 편집 예시는 관계를 성과로만 계산하지 않는 읽기다. 만남의 기쁨도 서로 가능한 시간과 방문 의사를 확인하는 데서 시작하며, 예고 없는 방문을 반갑게 받아들일 의무를 뜻하지 않는다.

### 읽는 관점

관계의 가치는 유용함만 아니라 함께 있음의 기쁨에서도 찾을 수 있다.

### 나에게 묻기

다시 만나 함께 시간을 보내고 싶은 사람은 누구인가?

### 주의할 점

기쁘게 맞이하라는 말이 원치 않는 방문을 받아들일 의무는 아니다.

### 인용 원문

> Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters?

### 출처

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · I.1.2

James Legge translation, The Chinese Classics; Project Gutenberg \#3330

— Confucius
en-US.description:
**Confucius · Analects · I.1.2**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

The opening of the Analects places the delight of visiting friends beside the pleasure of learning.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

A reunion need not produce useful information or solve a problem to have value. Recalling shared learning and hearing how each person’s views changed can matter in themselves. This editorial example resists measuring a relationship only by its output. Enjoyment still begins with checking whether both people want and can make time for the visit. The saying offers a welcome image of companionship, not an obligation to receive an unwanted or unannounced guest.

### A perspective

A relationship can matter for shared presence as well as practical help.

### Reflect

Whom would I like to meet again simply to spend time together?

### Keep in mind

Hospitality does not require accepting an unwanted visit.

### Source quotation

> Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters?

### Source

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · I.1.2

James Legge translation, The Chinese Classics; Project Gutenberg \#3330

論語の冒頭は、学ぶ喜びに続いて遠来の友を迎える喜びを語る。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

久しぶりの再会は有用情報や問題解決がなくても価値を持ちうる。共に学んだことを思い出し、考えの変化を聞くこと自体に意味がある。この編集例は関係を成果だけで測らない。喜びも互いの希望や時間の確認から始まる。望まない訪問や予告のない来客まで歓迎する義務ではない。

### 読みの視点

役に立つことだけでなく、一緒にいる喜びにも関係の価値がある。

### 自分への問い

ただ時間を共にしたくて、また会いたい人は誰か。

### 注意点

望まない訪問を受け入れる義務を意味しない。

### 出典の原文

> Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters?

— Confucius
en-US.description:
**Confucius · Analects · XII.23**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Asked about friendship, Confucius joins faithful advice to a limit on continued persuasion.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Repeatedly recommending a different hobby class because you prefer it can turn advice into pressure to change a friend’s choice. Asking whether advice is wanted, explaining the reason and respecting the decision offers another approach. This editorial example concerns an ordinary difference in preference. It is not a rule for abandoning someone in immediate danger. What support is appropriate depends on the situation, and care need not mean replacing the other person’s judgment with one’s own.

### A perspective

Care can be distinguished from taking over another person’s choices.

### Reflect

When does my advice become repeated pressure rather than help?

### Keep in mind

An immediate danger may require practical support rather than simply ending the conversation.

### Source quotation

> Faithfully admonish your friend, and skillfully lead him on. If you find him impracticable, stop. Do not disgrace yourself.

### Source

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · XII.23

自分の好みと違う趣味の講座を友人が選んだとき、別案を繰り返し勧めれば選択変更の圧力になりうる。助言を望むか尋ね、理由を説明して決定を尊重する方法もある。この編集例は通常の好みの違いを扱い、目前の危険にある人を放置する規則ではない。適切な支援は状況によって異なり、配慮は判断の代行に限られない。

### 自分への問い

私の助言はいつ、助けより繰り返す圧力になるか。

### 注意点

切迫した危険には、会話をやめるだけでなく具体的な支援が必要なこともある。

### 出典の原文

朋友選的興趣課不同於你的偏好，反覆推薦別班可能把建議變成改選壓力。先問是否想聽意見、說明理由並尊重決定，是另一方法。這個編輯例子談一般偏好差異，不是讓人處於立即危險也放手不管的規則。適當支援依情境而異，關心不必等於代替對方判斷。

我的勸告何時變成反覆施壓，而非幫助？

遇到迫切危險時，可能需要實際支援，而不只是停止談話。

en-US.description:
**Francis Bacon · Essays · Of Friendship, second fruit**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Bacon’s second fruit of friendship is help with judgment and affairs, beyond emotional relief.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

“Please listen for now” and “Help me find gaps in this plan” ask for different things. Naming the need can help a friend know whether comfort or examination is wanted. This editorial example makes room for empathy and another perspective without assuming they are interchangeable. Where a decision requires specialist knowledge, friendship does not supply that expertise automatically. A confident friend’s advice still needs relevant evidence, and useful disagreement need not diminish the relationship.

### A perspective

Friendship may include both sympathy and a different view.

### Reflect

How can I distinguish asking a friend for agreement from asking for advice?

### Keep in mind

Closeness does not guarantee expertise or sound judgment.

### Source quotation

> But when all is done, the help of good counsel, is that which setteth business straight.

**Ralph Waldo Emerson · Essays · Friendship, paragraph containing “Wait until the necessary”**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Emerson stresses embodying friendship rather than trying to force intimacy.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

If you value a friend remembering important occasions, you might note and ask about something they said mattered to them. That is one concrete way to practice the attention you hope to receive. It does not create a claim to repayment. This editorial case distinguishes being a friend from investing kindness for a guaranteed return. Also notice whether care is becoming a one-sided obligation; acting generously need not mean ignoring one’s own limits or the other person’s freedom.

### A perspective

We can ask whether we practice the qualities we want to receive.

### Reflect

What act of friendship I have wanted from someone could I offer first?

### Keep in mind

Being a good friend does not guarantee reciprocal friendship.

### Source quotation

### Context

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

If repeated lateness has hurt, describe what happened and why it mattered rather than pretending it did not. Give the friend room to explain and consider together how to arrange the next meeting. ### A perspective

This can prompt a candid conversation undertaken for the relationship’s sake.

### Reflect

What conversation should I stop avoiding while still respecting my friend?

### Keep in mind

Confidence in a bond does not justify ignoring consent or boundaries.

### Source quotation

약속에 반복해서 늦는 일이 서운했다면 아무렇지 않은 척하기보다 어떤 상황에서 무엇이 어려웠는지 말할 수 있다. 상대에게도 설명할 기회를 주고 다음 약속을 어떻게 정할지 함께 살피는 방식이다. 이 편집 예시의 용기는 큰소리를 내는 데 있지 않고 중요한 문제를 존중하며 다루는 데 있다. 관계가 오래되었다는 이유로 상대의 경계를 넘거나 대화를 강요해도 된다는 뜻은 아니다.

### 맥락

소로는 좋은 사람과 함께 있어도 곧 피곤해지며, 혼자 있는 시간이 자신에게 유익하다고 말한다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

친구와 즐겁게 만난 뒤에도 혼자 읽거나 쉬는 시간이 필요할 수 있다. 다음 약속을 정할 때 그 필요를 말하면 만남을 싫어한다는 뜻과 거리를 둘 수 있다. 이 편집 예시는 가까움과 간격이 반드시 반대가 아님을 보여 준다. 그러나 혼자 있고 싶은 선택과 만나고 싶은데 만날 수 없는 상태는 다르다. 모든 사람에게 같은 양의 고독을 권하는 원칙으로 삼지 않는다.

### 읽는 관점

우정에 필요한 간격을 결핍이 아니라 회복의 일부로 볼 수 있다.

친구와 잘 지내기 위해 내게 필요한 혼자만의 시간은 얼마인가?

> I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.

en-US.description:
**Henry David Thoreau · Walden · Solitude**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Thoreau says that even good company can tire him and that much solitude is wholesome for him.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

After an enjoyable visit, someone may still want time alone to read or rest. Naming that need when arranging another meeting can distinguish it from rejection of the friend. This editorial example shows that closeness and intervals need not be opposites. Chosen solitude differs from wanting company that is unavailable, however. The passage does not prescribe the same amount of aloneness for everyone; the meaning of the interval depends on choice, circumstances and the people involved.

### A perspective

Space within friendship may support renewal rather than signal failure.

### Reflect

What time alone helps me return to my friends with attention?

### Keep in mind

Chosen solitude differs from unwanted isolation.

### Source quotation

> I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.

### Source

[Walden](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/205/pg205-images.html) · Solitude

English original (1854); Project Gutenberg \#205

### 文脈

ソローは良い仲間といても疲れることがあり、一人の時間が自分に有益だと述べる。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

楽しい再会の後も、一人で読む・休む時間が必要なことがある。次の予定を決める際に伝えれば、友人を拒む意味と区別できる。この編集例は親密さと間隔が必ずしも反対ではないと示す。ただし選んだ孤独と、会いたくても会えない状態は異なる。全員に同じ独りの量を勧めず、選択・状況・当事者により意味を考える。

### 読みの視点

友情の中の距離を、欠如より回復の一部として見られる。

### 自分への問い

友に注意を向けて戻るために、どんな一人の時間が必要か。

### 注意点

選んだ孤独と望まない孤立は異なる。

### 出典の原文

> I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.

ko.description:
**메리 울스턴크래프트 · 여성의 권리 옹호 · 2장**

앞면은 아래 인용 원문을 직접 번역한 문장입니다. 해설·질문·관계는 편집 내용입니다.

### 맥락

울스턴크래프트는 남편의 열정을 유지하려고 애정을 감추라는 조언을 비판하며, 격정에서 존중과 우정으로의 변화를 말한다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

처음 만날 때의 강렬한 설렘이 줄어도 서로의 선택을 존중하고 어려운 일을 함께 상의하는 관계가 생길 수 있다. 이 편집 예시는 감정의 강도 하나로 관계 전체를 평가하지 않는 방식이다. 울스턴크래프트가 비판한 것은 애정을 전략적으로 감추어 열정을 유지하려는 교육의 맥락이라는 점을 남겨 둔다. 모든 사랑이 같은 순서로 바뀐다거나 오래된 관계를 무조건 유지해야 한다는 법칙은 아니다.

### 읽는 관점

연애의 강도만으로 관계의 가치를 판단하고 있지는 않은지 물을 수 있다.

### 나에게 묻기

처음의 설렘이 달라진 뒤에도 함께 기르고 싶은 관계의 성질은 무엇인가?

### 주의할 점

여기서 사랑은 주로 연애의 격정이다. 모든 형태의 사랑이 반드시 사라진다는 증명은 아니다.

### 인용 원문

> Love, from its very nature, must be transitory.

### 출처

[A Vindication of the Rights of Woman](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3420/pg3420.html) · Chapter II

English original, 1792; Project Gutenberg \#3420

en-US.title:
Love, from its very nature, must be transitory.
— Mary Wollstonecraft
en-US.description:
**Mary Wollstonecraft · A Vindication of the Rights of Woman · Chapter II**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Wollstonecraft criticizes advice to conceal affection to sustain a husband’s passion and favors a transition toward respect and friendship.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

As initial excitement changes, a relationship may develop shared deliberation and respect for each person’s choices. This editorial scene avoids judging the whole relationship by emotional intensity alone. Keep in view Wollstonecraft’s criticism of advice to conceal affection strategically to sustain passion. The example does not establish one sequence for every kind of love or require preserving every long relationship. The quality of respect and present circumstances still need to be examined.

### A perspective

We can question whether intensity alone measures an intimate relationship.

### Reflect

What qualities would I want to cultivate after the first excitement changes?

### Keep in mind

Love here primarily means romantic passion; this is not proof that every form of love must vanish.

### Source quotation

> Love, from its very nature, must be transitory.

### Source

[A Vindication of the Rights of Woman](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3420/pg3420.html) · Chapter II

English original, 1792; Project Gutenberg \#3420

ja.title:
恋愛は、その本性からして移ろうものである。
— メアリ・ウルストンクラフト
ja.description:
**メアリ・ウルストンクラフト · 女性の権利の擁護 · 第2章**

表面は下記の引用原文からの独自訳です。解説・問い・関係は編集によるものです。

### 文脈

ウルストンクラフトは夫の情熱を保つため愛情を隠せという助言を批判し、尊重と友情への移行を重んじる。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

初めの高揚が変わっても、選択の尊重や困難を相談する関係が育つことがある。この編集例は感情の強度だけで全体を評価しない。情熱を保つため愛情を戦略的に隠せという助言への批判を原文の背景として残す。すべての愛が同じ順で変わる法則でも、長い関係を必ず維持すべき要求でもない。現在の尊重や条件の検討は必要である。

### 読みの視点

関係の価値を情熱の強さだけで測っていないか問える。

### 自分への問い

最初のときめきが変わった後も、共に育てたい性質は何か。

### 注意点

ここでの愛は主に恋愛の情熱であり、すべての愛が消える証明ではない。

### 出典の原文

> Love, from its very nature, must be transitory.

### 出典

[A Vindication of the Rights of Woman](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3420/pg3420.html) · Chapter II

English original, 1792; Project Gutenberg \#3420

zh-TW.description:
**瑪麗・沃斯通克拉夫特 · 女權辯護 · 第2章**

沃斯通克拉夫特批評以隱藏愛意維持丈夫熱情的建議，並重視轉向尊重與友誼。

### 從今日案例閱讀・編輯解說

初期興奮改變後，關係可能發展出共同商議與尊重各自選擇。這個編輯場景不只以情緒強度評價整段關係，也保留原文批判為維持激情而策略性隱藏愛意的脈絡。例子不建立每種愛都循相同順序的法則，也不要求維持所有長久關係，仍須檢視當下尊重與條件。

可以反問自己，是否只以激情強度衡量親密關係。

### 自我提問

最初的心動改變之後，我仍想共同培養什麼品質？

### 注意事項

此處的愛主要指戀愛激情，不是證明各種愛都必然消失。

### 出處原文

> Love, from its very nature, must be transitory.

### 出處

English original, 1792; Project Gutenberg \#3420

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Wollstonecraft criticizes an education that narrows women’s hearts and minds in a vain effort to prevent sorrow and error.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

After one broken arrangement, refusing every future plan may remove opportunities for companionship along with the risk of disappointment. Unconditionally trusting someone who repeatedly lies is not the necessary alternative. This editorial example avoids an all-or-nothing model of trust. Small verifiable commitments and boundaries can inform further judgment. It does not tell anyone to endure abuse or ongoing deception; openness to a relationship and attention to evidence can be considered together.

### A perspective

We can examine what perfect protection from disappointment would cost intimacy and self-respect.

### Reflect

What fear is narrowing my capacity to trust or love too much?

### Keep in mind

This is not advice to endure repeated deception or abuse; trust still needs evidence and boundaries.
